[Film still.] Single-channel video projection shot on 16 mm Kodak Vision 3 500T film, wire gauze, plaster, cardboard, found objects, acrylic paint, confetti, wood, image prints, and celluloid film. 12 min 30 sec. A Secret Portrait of Wan Hoi-Ling (2025) reimagines the life of Wan Hoi-Ling, a pioneering but little-known female director and screenwriter who worked across Hong Kong and Singapore, creating anti-imperialist, anti-colonial films. In this interview, artist Elsa Wong reflects on how she transposed her research into the film’s three-part narrative, working with a variety of materials and techniques, from sourcing found objects to crafting dioramas, experimenting with 16mm film, and developing a multi-language soundtrack. Seeking an alternative to stereotypical portrayals of Wan as a tragic heroine, Elsa offers the viewer an empathetic vision of a woman moving through love, ambition, and loss. TO SEE Image still from Blue Velvet (1986, David Lynch) Asian Film Archive: Edward Yang’s Four Favourite Films Following up from a full retrospective of Edward Yang’s iconic oeuvre, the Asian Film Archive (AFA) presents 4 of the auteur’s favourite classic films: Nostalghia (1983) by Andrei Tarkovsky), My American Uncle (1980) by Alain Resnais, Blue Velvet (1986) by David Lynch and Aguirre, the Wrath of God (1972) by Werner Herzog, each having influenced Yang’s attitudes and approaches to his own practice. source_title: Blueprints For An Ephemeral and Affective Experience
source_description: My first encounter with the Asian Film Archive (AFA) was completely serendipitous. When I was at the Cannes Film Festival in 2022, I was able to catch a screening of Mike de Leon’s Itim, as part of the Cannes Classics selection. Having seen many older films before, it was not my first time watching one […] My first encounter with the Asian Film Archive (AFA) was completely serendipitous. When I was at the Cannes Film Festival in 2022, I was able to catch a screening of Mike de Leon’s Itim , as part of the Cannes Classics selection. Having seen many older films before, it was not my first time watching one with a ‘restored’ label. The magic of film restoration did not fully dawn on me until I watched Itim though. I was dumbfounded by the beauty of the restoration carried out by the film restoration laboratory, L’Immagine Ritrovata, as the version that I watched a long time ago was blotchy and was of very low-quality. I found that the restoration had maintained the atmosphere and visual signature of the film while elevating the technical ingenuity of the camerawork. Image stills from Itim (1976, Mike de Leon) This screening of Itim , and the entire Cannes Classics programme, opened me up to the world of moving image heritage. It reminded me of what my secondary school history teacher emphasised on the importance of learning about the past, that history is crucial to navigating the present and future. Beyond the familiar genre conventions, Itim echoes this sentiment as an...

source_title: Asian Cinema Digest #44
source_description: This issue of the Asian Cinema Digest focuses on Southeast, East and West Asian cinema. Delve into the works of Vietnamese filmmakers such as Nguyễn Trinh Thi and Trinh Thi Minh Hà, and film and video installations of Tulapop Saenjaroen. To celebrate the Lunar New Year, revisit some works from Hong Kong Cinema available on […] This issue of the Asian Cinema Digest focuses on Southeast, East and West Asian cinema. Delve into the works of Vietnamese filmmakers such as Nguyễn Trinh Thi and Trinh Thi Minh Hà, and film and video installations of Tulapop Saenjaroen. To celebrate the Lunar New Year, revisit some works from Hong Kong Cinema available on Criterion Channel. Also featured are the works of West Asian directors Bahram Beyzaie, Otar Iosseliani and Sergei Parajanov. WATCH Images de Chine (1901-1904) by Auguste François Shot at the end of the Qing dynasty, French consul, Auguste François (aka 方苏雅) captured people’s daily life in the streets of Kunming, Yunnan, using a camera given by Léon Gaumont. Cinémathèque Française and the CNC heritage department have scanned the nitrate films footage captured by François. Stream it now on Cinémathèque Française’s online platform, Henri. Co-founded by filmmakers Rithy Panh and Pannakar Ieu, this center plays a crucial role in preserving the country’s audiovisual archives. The handover of the painting, received with gratitude, highlights Danhôo’s commitment to memory […] The French painter Danhôo has recently donated one of his works, titled Partage (Sharing), to the Bophana Center in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. Co-founded by filmmakers Rithy Panh and Pannakar Ieu, this center plays a crucial role in preserving the country’s audiovisual archives. The handover of the painting, received with gratitude, highlights Danhôo’s commitment to memory and cultural heritage. In addition, the artist is further deepening his involvement by becoming an ambassador for the Fragments #KH50 project. This program, led by the Fragmentis Vitae Asia association, aims to collect and share the testimonies of Cambodian families who lived under the Khmer Rouge regime over the past 50 years. Through this gesture and commitment, Danhôo puts his art at the service of transmission and dialogue. source_description: Phnom Penh, October 25, 2024 – Bophana Audiovisual Resource Center will join the global community in celebrating World Day for Audiovisual Heritage on October 27th, 2024. This important day, designated by UNESCO, aims to raise awareness about the significance of preserving audiovisual materials for future generations. As part of the commemoration, Bophana Center invites individuals, […] Phnom Penh, October 25, 2024 – Bophana Audiovisual Resource Center will join the global community in celebrating World Day for Audiovisual Heritage on October 27th, 2024 . This important day, designated by UNESCO, aims to raise awareness about the significance of preserving audiovisual materials for future generations. As part of the commemoration, Bophana Center invites individuals, institutions, and the general public across Cambodia to reflect on the value of their own audiovisual collections, which may be stored in homes, offices, or warehouses. Audiovisual materials such as film reels, audio and video cassettes, vinyl records, reel-to-reel tapes, and photographs hold a wealth of historical and cultural significance. These materials, however, are highly vulnerable to decay if not properly preserved. As part of its mission, Bophana Center encourages everyone to pay attention to the condition of these invaluable assets. source_description: Exciting News from Bophana Center! We are thrilled to share that Mr. CHEA Sopheap, Director of Bophana Audiovisual Resource Center, recently delivered a captivating presentation highlighting our ongoing efforts in audiovisual archives preservation and accessibility. Moreover, we are proud to continue nurturing the filmmaking talents of Cambodian youth to document their communities. In addition, Jason Sanders from the BAMPFA team presented on the collaborative work between BAMPFA and Bophana Center at the “FIAF 2024 Symposium: Film Archives in the Global South” held between April 21-26, 2024. source_description: Bophana Audiovisual Resource Center and UNESCO would like to announcethat both institutions will work together to implement the project “Building Capacity for Indigenous Youth and Establishing Indigenous Audiovisual Archives Through Wiki-tools in Cambodia” Bophana Audiovisual Resource Center and UNESCO would like to announcethat both institutions will work together to implement the project “ Building Capacity for Indigenous Youth and Establishing Indigenous Audiovisual Archives Through Wiki-tools in Cambodia” from July 2021 until June 2022 under the organizational grant of Wikimedia Foundation . The Project aims to use Wikimedia tools and platforms to build an open access Indigenous audiovisual archive to preserve, protect and revitalize indigenous languages in Cambodia. The project will provide a capacity-building training program to 30 indigenous youth from different indigenous communities of Ratanakiri, Cambodia, on documentary filmmaking from the theory to the practice. The indigenous youth will learn the whole process of documentary film production (pre-production, production and post-production) so that they are able to produce audiovisual materials in their own languages, about the lives and culture of their community. source_description: App-learning on Khmer Rouge History is an application that allows users to learn the Khmer Rouge through smart devices (mart phones and/or tablets) which has free online access for all. As a proposed reparation project in front of Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia, the objective of the project is to educate the youth […] App-learning on Khmer Rouge History is an application that allows users to learn the Khmer Rouge through smart devices (mart phones and/or tablets) which has free online access for all. As a proposed reparation project in front of Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia, the objective of the project is to educate the youth on Khmer Rouge History as well as to raise awareness about justice, human rights and peace hosting an exchange between Khmer Rouge survivors and the young people. The information and archived media existing in the app was validated by Cambodian and international experts of Khmer Rouge History. Bophana Center is the creator of the project and focuses on teaching and understanding Cambodian History and culture which it has done since its foundation, through archives, movies, documentaries… App-learning on Khmer Rouge History is a way to preserve national memory and to reach the younger generations. This project was Funded by the European Union and REI Foundation Limited. source_title: “Archives at Risk: Protecting the World’s Identities – Memories of Indochina”
source_description: Bophana Center in collaboration with French Institute and Center for Khmer Studies (CKS) launches a week-long screening event. Since 2007, October 27th has been set by UNESCO as the World Day for Audiovisual Heritage to spotlight archives institutions, giving them an opportunity to showcase their works in celebration of the world audiovisual heritage. During one […] Bophana Center in collaboration with French Institute and Center for Khmer Studies (CKS) launches a week-long screening event. Since 2007, October 27th has been set by UNESCO as the World Day for Audiovisual Heritage to spotlight archives institutions, giving them an opportunity to showcase their works in celebration of the world audiovisual heritage. During one week, Bophana Center and the Institut français du Cambodge are collaborating to offer, for the first time in Cambodia, public screenings of rare movies on Indochina which were recently restored by the French CNC (Centre national du cinéma et de l’image animée). This movie selection aims to share the history and memories of the people of Indochina and also to raise the question of people’s identity under colonialism. The screenings will start on the World Day for Audiovisual Heritage and will last for one week. On the 27th of October, for the opening screening, Bophana Center will welcome Dr. Henri Locard for a lecture on Indochina; and on the 4th of November, for the closing screening, Ms. Khuon Vichheka will give a lecture, “Battambang during WWII”....

source_description: Akhir-akhir ini, dua warna mendadak jadi penanda politik: hijau dari jaket ojek online bernama Affan Kurniawan yang tubuhnya terlindas mobil polisi, dan pink dari hijab seorang ibu yang berdiri melawan aparat yang bernama Ana. Dua peristiwa ini beredar cepat di media sosial, menyisakan jejak visual yang lebih kuat dari narasi … Akhir-akhir ini, dua warna mendadak jadi penanda politik: hijau dari jaket ojek online bernama Affan Kurniawan yang tubuhnya terlindas mobil polisi, dan pink dari hijab seorang ibu yang berdiri melawan aparat yang bernama Ana. Dua peristiwa ini beredar cepat di media sosial, menyisakan jejak visual yang lebih kuat dari narasi panjang. Imbasnya jelas: desain protes tidak lagi bergantung pada poster atau tipografi, tapi bisa lahir spontan dari warna, dari momen, dari fragmen keseharian yang berubah jadi simbol. Apakah simbol selalu harus berupa gambar? Keraguan ini muncul ketika kita melihat bahwa warna sesederhana itu dapat menjadi tanda perlawanan. Dua warna ini berubah menjadi simbol cair, lahir spontan dari tubuh sosial. Di titik ini, kita belajar bahwa subversi visual tak selalu berbentuk lambang warna pun bisa menjadi penanda resistensi. Perbedaan penting ada pada sifat simbolnya. Ada simbol seolah terkunci seperti swastika: satu makna yang tak bisa ditebus, terikat selamanya oleh sejarah. source_description: Asal-Usul Tulisan ini merupakan tawaran dalam mengelola pembelajaran formal desain komunikasi visual (DKV). Tawaran tersebut hasil dari pengalaman dalam memberi lokakarya desain layout dan mengampu kelas pilihan Desain Layout. Lokakarya desain layout yang saya berikan untuk pers mahasiswa. Lokakarya tersebut biasanya diikuti beberapa orang, terutama bagian layouter di media pers mahasiswa … Asal-Usul Tulisan ini merupakan tawaran dalam mengelola pembelajaran formal desain komunikasi visual (DKV). Tawaran tersebut hasil dari pengalaman dalam memberi lokakarya desain layout dan mengampu kelas pilihan Desain Layout. Lokakarya desain layout yang saya berikan untuk pers mahasiswa. Lokakarya tersebut biasanya diikuti beberapa orang, terutama bagian layouter di media pers mahasiswa dan redaksi. Biasanya tak lebih dari lima orang peserta dengan jumlah pertemuan lima hingga tujuh kali. Sebelum dibuka mata kuliah pilihan Desain Layout di tempat saya mengajar (DKV ISI Yogyakarta) pernah ada mata kuliah dengan nama Komputer Grafis. Dari namanya memperlihatkan jejak era pembelajarannya. Nama “Komputer Grafis” sudah ada sebelum saya bergabung di Prodi DKV ISI Yogyakarta (2005). Dalam pembelajaran Komputer Grafis ada tiga pilihan software yakni Adobe Photoshop, Quarkxpress yang kemudian menjadi Page Maker lalu Adobe InDesign, dan Adobe Illustrator. Singkatnya, nama “Komputer Grafis” menggambarkan pentingnya mahasiswa mempelajari software saat itu. Jalan beberapa tahun nama kuliah...

source_description: “Dalam era media sosial ini, orang-orang terkenal dan ambisius sering kali mencari pengakuan publik dari orang-orang yang hampir tidak mereka kenal. Namun, penting untuk diingat sesuatu yang sering dilupakan: sejuta orang bisa salah secara fantastis,” tulis Erik Kessels, seorang seniman Belanda, dalam bukunya “Failed It!: How to turn mistakes into … “Dalam era media sosial ini, orang-orang terkenal dan ambisius sering kali mencari pengakuan publik dari orang-orang yang hampir tidak mereka kenal. Namun, penting untuk diingat sesuatu yang sering dilupakan: sejuta orang bisa salah secara fantastis,” tulis Erik Kessels, seorang seniman Belanda, dalam bukunya “Failed It!: How to turn mistakes into ideas and other advice for successfully screwing up.” Erik menyoroti bagaimana di era modern ini, opini yang dianggap sesuai dapat dengan mudah menjadi populer dalam skala besar, meningkatkan risiko bagi ide-ide baru yang sering dipraduga sebagai pemikiran yang banal. source_title: Memaknai Desain Grafis sebagai Gagasan Politis
source_description: Jika modal dan tugas desainer adalah memecahkan masalah yang berkaitan dengan banyak pihak, maka desain pula adalah tindakan politik. source_title: Kemungkinan Sejarah Baru Desain Grafis di Normal Baru
source_description: Sebuah telaah kemungkinan sejarah baru desain grafis di Normal Baru melalui pembacaan peristiwa-peristiwa sejarah dunia dan kaitannya dengan desain grafis. Tulisan ini mendasarkan pembacaannya pada buku Desain Grafis Indonesia Dalam Pusaran Desain Grafis Dunia (2015). “Peran desain grafis dalam aktivisme dapat lebih dalam daripada sekadar poster dan T-shirt,” kata antropolog desain … Sebuah telaah kemungkinan sejarah baru desain grafis di Normal Baru melalui pembacaan peristiwa-peristiwa sejarah dunia dan kaitannya dengan desain grafis. Tulisan ini mendasarkan pembacaannya pada buku Desain Grafis Indonesia Dalam Pusaran Desain Grafis Dunia (2015). “ Peran desain grafis dalam aktivisme dapat lebih dalam daripada sekadar poster dan T-shirt ,” kata antropolog desain Stanford Dori Tunstall. Desain grafis tidak hanya menyoal visual yang tangible , tapi juga tentang perancangan ‘nilai sosial’ yang disepakati bersama oleh suatu pergerakan aktivisme tanpa memberi sekat terhadap disiplin tertentu. Dalam ranah sosial, keprofesian desain memang bersinggungan dan berkombinasi dengan bidang maupun disiplin lain. Dan dalam sejarahnya, keprofesian desain grafis juga ‘hadir’ dalam peristiwa-peristiwa dunia, bahkan dalam taraf tertentu dapat memberi dampak nyata bagi perubahan sosial budaya masyarakat di berbagai belahan di dunia. source_title: Obituari Ayip Budiman
source_description: Arief ‘Ayip’ Budiman Minggu malam saya terima berita duka tersebut dari chat grup komunitas kecil kami. Kaget, karena sebelumnya ada berita duka juga terkait kawan lama. Sesaat setelahnya saya berusaha mengingat sosok Ayip. Secara pribadi saya tidak begitu kenal, namun dalam jejaring kami di asosiasi, organisasi, dan media ternyata Ayip dan … Arief ‘Ayip’ Budiman Minggu malam saya terima berita duka tersebut dari chat grup komunitas kecil kami. Kaget, karena sebelumnya ada berita duka juga terkait kawan lama. Sesaat setelahnya saya berusaha mengingat sosok Ayip. Secara pribadi saya tidak begitu kenal, namun dalam jejaring kami di asosiasi, organisasi, dan media ternyata Ayip dan saya cukup banyak berinteraksi. Saya mengingatnya lagi. Terakhir saya bertemu beliau di Agustus 2015, pada acara International Conference of Creative Industry (ICCI), diselenggarakan di Denpasar, Bali. Saya diundang untuk membicarakan topik ‘mapping’ profesi desain grafis dan memperkenalkan Desain Grafis Indonesia-DGI, organisai yang saya bantu kelola. Ayip membicarakan kegiatan kreatif inisiatifnya, sebuah proyek film. Ia memulai presentasinya dengan mengutip Bung Karno: “Negeri kita kaya, kaya, kaya-raya, saudara-saudara. Berjiwa besarlah, berimagination. Gali! Bekerja! Gali! Bekerja! source_description: Dari Nirmana Tulisan ini berawal dari usaha memahami kerja mendesain (dkv) dari sisi ruang dan ruang kosong. Umumnya mendesain, lebih spesifiknya desain tata letak, dipahami sebagai kegiatan menata berbagai unsur di ruang tertentu seperti halaman buku, surat kabar, undangan, iklan, dsb. Kerja mendesain lebih tertuju pada sisi yang terlihat, termasuk ruang. … Dari Nirmana Tulisan ini berawal dari usaha memahami kerja mendesain (dkv) dari sisi ruang dan ruang kosong. Umumnya mendesain, lebih spesifiknya desain tata letak, dipahami sebagai kegiatan menata berbagai unsur di ruang tertentu seperti halaman buku, surat kabar, undangan, iklan, dsb. Kerja mendesain lebih tertuju pada sisi yang terlihat, termasuk ruang. Rasa penasaran saya muncul manakala menjumpai penjelasan tentang ruang yang terdapat di halaman 127 buku “Nirmana Elemen-elemen Seni dan Desain” karya Sadjiman Ebdi Sanyoto penerbit (Jalasutra, cetakan II, September 2010). Pada paragraf pertama di halaman tersebut tertulis demikian with this post : “Setiap bentuk pasti menempati ruang. Oleh karena itu, ruang merupakan unsur rupa yang mesti ada, karena ruang merupakan tempat bentuk-bentuk berada (exist) . Dengan kata lain bahwa setiap bentuk pasti menempati ruang”. Dalam buku tersebut dijelaskan pula bahwa ada dua hal mendasar dalam Nirmana yaitu unsur dan prinsip. source_description: A collection of matchbox labels from around the world. Graphic design history of one of advertising’s smallest and most overlooked formats. One of the smallest canvases in the history of advertising, matchbox labels were produced economically and at high volume. Varying in size from a postage stamp to a playing card, these modest formats demanded maximum visual clarity. The designers had to reduce ideas to flat colour, simple iconography, and type that could be read at a glance. The printing constraints were severe. Most labels were produced by lithography, often in limited colour runs and on cheap paper stock. This forced designers to produce refined and constrained graphic design in the industrial era. The first friction match is believed to have been sold in 1827, following several prototypes developed by John Walker, a pharmacist from Stockton-on-Tees. As matches spread across the world, so did the labels that housed them. By the mid-nineteenth century, match manufacture had become a significant industry, with factories across Europe, Asia, and America producing matches by the billion. With competition between manufacturers, the label was one of the few points of difference available. Like all packaging, it had to identify the brand, communicate safety information, and catch the eye, all within a rectangle small enough to fit in a pocket. Among the highest-output producers, Czechoslovakia, the Soviet Union, and India each developed their own distinct visual styles....

source_medium: Design Archive Feature; Members Only Content; Regional Histories; Typography & Type Design
source_description: 60 examples of Czech typography from Typografia Vol. 20 (1909). Czech commercial printing at the crossroads of Art Nouveau and early modernism, with work by Methoděj Kaláb, Otokar Císař, Karel Dyrink and many more. As I have collected more issues of Typografia, I have been visually learning about the advancement and stylistic development of Typography in the Czech Republic. I have scanned in a few hundred samples of the inserted sheets. Most of them have never surfaced on the internet or ever had presence in design books, so it gives me great satisfaction to have these fantastic typographic pieces of history documented. From the 1909 issues, I have scanned in at high-resolution sixty of the sample sheets from this (twentieth) volume. I have also scanned in lots more for future articles too. Knihtiskaři Novotný a Příhoda Business Stationery Knihtiskaři Novotný a Příhoda business stationery and printed matter specimens from Královské Vinohrady, Prague. Published in Typografia, Vol. XX, 1909. The designs feature ornamental typography and stylised Secession motifs integrated into practical commercial design. Keramická továrna Praha–Nusle Advertising Specimen Keramická továrna Praha–Nusle advertising specimen for a ceramic factory in Prague-Nusle. Published in Typografia, Vol. XX, 1909. source_title: 40 Examples of Czech Typography from 1907, Typografia
source_object_type: Design Archive Feature; Members Only Content; Regional Histories; Typography & Type Design
source_medium: Design Archive Feature; Members Only Content; Regional Histories; Typography & Type Design
source_description: 40 examples of Czech typography from Typografia Vol. 18 (1907). Czech commercial printing at the crossroads of Art Nouveau and early modernism, with work by Otokar Císař, Method Kaláb, and Mořic Novotný. Typografia was a Czech typography and printing journal first published in Prague in 1888. I have collected over 400 issues and continue to source the remaining missing volumes for the archive. Each issue included finely printed supplementary sheets featuring decorative commercial printing specimens, business stationery, advertisements, and typographic layouts, offering valuable examples of contemporary Czech typography and commercial printing practice. I have scanned in at high-resolution fourty of the sample sheets from the eighteenth volume in 1907. Linear Art Nouveau Advertisement Designs for Jan Hryzal and Václav Staroch Printing Works Art Nouveau advertisement and commercial designs for Jan Hryzal of Prague and the printing works of Václav Staroch in Žižkov. Published in Typografia, Vol. XVIII, Issue 7, 1907. Designed by Otokar Císař and printed by Adolf Dvořák at the Politika printing works in Prague. The restrained compositions and simplified geometric ornament reflect the decorative Art Nouveau and functional commercial typography. source_description: An overview of graphic design in 1900, exploring Art Nouveau, the Eckmann-Schrift typeface, the Steglitz Workshop, the Doves Press and more, illustrated with artefacts from the Design Reviewed archive. This is the first of a series of articles focusing on graphic design year by year, which I intend to go from 1900-2000.The series will be illustrated with artefacts from the archive, scanned inners (in which I don’t currently have any original material) and relevant quotes and reference for further reading. I will also be revisiting this series from time-to-time as I uncover more content and add further artefacts to the archive. The series will also help me find gaps in the archive, in which I feel documentation isn’t on the website, and information and key pieces to be uploaded and purchased as I go. Although 1900 was the first year I wanted to focus on, the previous few years had seen the emergence of the Art Nouveau movement , which is regarded as one of the first international art movements. It became an international style and had a major influence on the design of books, posters and typeface design. Across Europe its variations of style and terms include Jugendstil, Modernismo, Secession and Stile Floreale. source_title: The Central School of Arts and Crafts (Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980)
source_description: The Central School of Arts and Crafts, featured in Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980 by Ian McLaren and Tony Pritchard. Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980 Ian McLaren and Tony Pritchard Chapter two of ‘ Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980 ’ focuses attention on the leading design schools of this period. This extract highlights the importance that the Central School of Arts and Crafts played in establishing the connection between design education and the emerging professional practice. An examination of those teaching and studying here during the late 1940s and early 1950s indicates the impact the participants were having on the evolution of what would become the design curriculum in many of the art schools that followed. The Central School of Arts and Crafts Art and design in Britain owes a great deal to William Johnstone. The son of a modest farmer on the Scottish borders, he came to London via Edinburgh, Paris and California. When appointed to principalship of the Central School of Arts and Crafts (the Central) during the late 1940s, he assembled a remarkable staff team. As a result, because of Johnstone’s enthusiasm and methods, during the immediate post-war period, the Central was without question the most dynamic art school in the country. Its department of Book Production, headed by Jesse Collins, was instrumental in assisting the development of many of the designers who played key roles in the evolution of the discipline, which...

source_title: Dennis Bailey (Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980)
source_description: A profile of British designer Dennis Bailey, featured in Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980 by Ian McLaren and Tony Pritchard, exploring his early influences and role in shaping post-war modernist graphic design in Britain. Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980 Ian McLaren and Tony Pritchard ‘ Modernist Graphic Design in Britain 1945–1980 ’ was first published in hardback during 2024. As it sold out quickly the authors wish to broaden the readership in the education sector. In a series for Design Reviewed in collaboration with The Modernist Society, we will publish profiles of a number of lesser-known graphic designers featured in the book who helped shape Modernist graphic design in Britain during the post-war period. Coinciding with a second printing of the book in softback the series begins with an exploration of the work of a designer who embraced continental European Modernist design and helped develop the themes which make Modernism in Britain distinctive. Dennis Bailey Dennis was born on the South coast of England; and brought up in Worthing. He refers to being intrigued by amongst other things watching local signwriters. 1 Before the advent of decals and laser cutting, signwriters used the brush. So one can well imagine that Dennis’s typographic sensitivity was informed from an early age by watching this essentially craft based skill. source_description: A 1928 article on typographic carnival posters, originally in German, published in Typographische Mitteilungen, Vol 25, No 02, February 1928 This article is part of a series I will be adding to the website called Design Translated. Where I will scan and translate content featured in rare design magazines published between 1920 and 1940. Many of these texts have never been translated before. My goal is to offer fresh perspectives and shed light on forgotten information, designers, and imagery from this fascinating era. This article was originally written in German and English and published in Typographische Mitteilungen, Vol 25, No 02, February 1928 Colourful posters, designed by artists and artistically inclined individuals in every conceivable style and fashion, produced in lithography and offset printing, now decorate walls and notice boards. All sorts of striking motifs and personalities are depicted in order to catch the eye, to arouse curiosity and entice people. In contrast to this exuberance, the pure type poster—or one produced only with typographic material—however skilfully and richly arranged, often appears rather sober, even dull. Now the business of lithographic and offset printing is flourishing, but the book printer too may occasionally secure work, even if not always highly profitable. Invitations and admission tickets, programmes and costume emblems are required, and only the typesetter who approaches the task with imagination, vitality, and a lively,......
